_comment: Per-city data for Fairfax, VA. Anchor city — EV Electric's office is at 9488 Fairfax Blvd, physically inside the City of Fairfax. The home-market framing differs from satellite cities: not '10-15 min away,' but 'around the corner.' Used by scaffold-core-30-page.py.
name: Fairfax
distance_from_hq_phrase: Our shop is at 9488 Fairfax Blvd — physically inside the City of Fairfax
geographic_anchor_paragraph: Fairfax is our home market. Our shop is at 9488 Fairfax Blvd, right on the Route 50/29 corridor. The City of Fairfax sits between Mantua to the north, Kings Park to the south, Fair Oaks to the west, and the Mosby Woods / Old Town border to the east — a tight mix of postwar ranches, 1960s-1970s colonials, 1990s-2000s townhomes, and pockets of new construction.
audience_descriptor: Residential homeowners in Fairfax, VA and surrounding City-of-Fairfax neighborhoods including Old Town Fairfax, Mantua, Kings Park, Mosby Woods, Country Club Hills, Fair Oaks, Fair Lakes, Fairfax Corner, Penderbrook, and Greenbriar.

housing_patterns.title: 1950s-1970s split-levels & ranches
housing_patterns.neighborhood_examples: Mosby Woods, Country Club Hills, neighborhoods bordering Old Town
housing_patterns.context_paragraph: Built with 100-amp panels and circuits sized for the appliances of the era — toaster, fridge, color TV, a window unit if you were lucky. Fast-forward to 2026: induction range, central AC, two refrigerators, a tankless water heater, and an EV charger in the garage. Modern load patterns overwhelm circuits the original builder never planned for.
housing_patterns.symptoms: persistent breaker trips, warm outlets, dimming lights when large appliances start.

housing_patterns.title: 1960s-1980s colonials & traditionals
housing_patterns.neighborhood_examples: Mantua, Kings Park, older Greenbriar blocks
housing_patterns.context_paragraph: 200-amp service but wired with the now-deprecated aluminum branch wiring for a window in the mid-1970s, or with GFCI gaps in kitchens and bathrooms that predate the 1996 code requirement.
housing_patterns.symptoms: outlets that worked yesterday and don't today, intermittent power loss to one room, GFCIs that trip the moment a hairdryer plugs in.

housing_patterns.title: 1990s-2020s townhomes & newer detached
housing_patterns.neighborhood_examples: Fair Oaks, Fair Lakes, Fairfax Corner, Penderbrook
housing_patterns.context_paragraph: Newer homes are not exempt. AFCI breakers (the arc-fault interrupters required by modern code) are sensitive by design and trip on any noisy load. Smart-home wiring done by the previous owner's "handy friend" can leave neutral wires bonded incorrectly.
housing_patterns.symptoms: failed dimmers, dead three-way switches, outlets that test fine but won't hold a plug.

troubleshooting.summary: Lights flicker when the AC or fridge kicks on
troubleshooting.body: Voltage drop. Often a loose neutral at the meter base or a damaged feeder. Common in older Mantua and Country Club Hills homes built before 1980 — the service entrance is reaching the end of its life. Worth diagnosing soon: persistent voltage drops shorten the life of every motor in your house.

troubleshooting.summary: A breaker keeps tripping (more than once a week)
troubleshooting.body: The breaker is doing its job — something's wrong upstream. Usually an overloaded circuit (new microwave + toaster on the same line), a short in a wall outlet, or a failed breaker itself. We trace which of the three in 30-60 minutes.

troubleshooting.summary: An outlet or switch plate feels warm to the touch
troubleshooting.body: Stop using the circuit and call us today. Heat at a connection means resistance, and resistance behind drywall is how house fires start. Most common in 1960s-1980s Kings Park and Mantua colonials with original wire-nut splices in junction boxes.

troubleshooting.summary: You smell burning plastic or "hot" electrical odor
troubleshooting.body: Treat this as urgent. Shut off the breaker for the affected area if you can identify it. We triage these calls to the earliest slot — typically same-day in Fairfax since our shop is right here. The cause is almost always overheated insulation at a loose connection.

troubleshooting.summary: Half your house has power, half doesn't
troubleshooting.body: An open neutral at the service entrance. Serious condition — it can fluctuate voltage between 50V and 200V and damage electronics. We test each leg of the panel and identify the failure point. Often a utility-side issue but we confirm before calling Dominion Energy.

troubleshooting.summary: Your EV charger throttles, trips, or warms the outlet
troubleshooting.body: EV charging puts continuous 30-50 amp draw on circuits that older Fairfax homes weren't designed for. The cause is usually upstream of the charger — a feeder, a breaker, or a connection that can't sustain the load. Common in Fair Oaks and Penderbrook townhomes where owners added a Level 2 charger to a pre-2010 panel.

most_common_problem_paragraph.troubleshooting: Two patterns dominate. In 1950s-1970s homes (Mosby Woods, Country Club Hills), the most common issue is circuit overload from modern appliances on original circuits. In 1960s-1980s homes (Mantua, Kings Park), the most common issue is intermittent power loss from aging connections in outlet boxes, panels, or junction boxes hidden in walls.

specific_problems_neighborhood_phrase.troubleshooting: Fairfax City and the surrounding Fair Oaks corridor have one of the highest EV adoption rates in Northern Virginia.
